import pandas as pd

# Load source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length3_34/training_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length3_34/training_1.csv"

df0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)
df1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)

# The source tables have wide format with years as columns.
# We need to UNPIVOT (melt) both tables to long format with columns: Country Name, Country Code, Year, Value

# Melt source0 for Rural Value
df0_melt = df0.melt(
    id_vars=['Country Name', 'Country Code', 'Indicator Name', 'Indicator Code'],
    var_name='Year',
    value_name='Rural Value'
)

# Filter only rows where Indicator Name corresponds to Rural population (% of total population)
df0_melt = df0_melt[df0_melt['Indicator Name'] == 'Rural population (% of total population)']

# Melt source1 for Electricity Value
df1_melt = df1.melt(
    id_vars=['Country Name', 'Country Code', 'Indicator Name', 'Indicator Code'],
    var_name='Year',
    value_name='Electricity Value'
)

# Filter only rows where Indicator Name corresponds to Access to electricity (% of population)
df1_melt = df1_melt[df1_melt['Indicator Name'] == 'Access to electricity (% of population)']

# Drop columns not needed after filtering
df0_melt = df0_melt[['Country Name', 'Country Code', 'Year', 'Rural Value']]
df1_melt = df1_melt[['Country Name', 'Country Code', 'Year', 'Electricity Value']]

# Merge the two melted dataframes on Country Name, Country Code, and Year
df_merged = pd.merge(df0_melt, df1_melt, on=['Country Name', 'Country Code', 'Year'], how='outer')

# Convert Year to string type to match target schema
df_merged['Year'] = df_merged['Year'].astype(str)

# Convert values to string type as per target schema
df_merged['Rural Value'] = df_merged['Rural Value'].astype(str)
df_merged['Electricity Value'] = df_merged['Electricity Value'].astype(str)

# Replace 'nan' strings with actual NaN for better representation
df_merged['Rural Value'] = df_merged['Rural Value'].replace('nan', pd.NA)
df_merged['Electricity Value'] = df_merged['Electricity Value'].replace('nan', pd.NA)

# Reorder columns to match target schema
Target3_34 = df_merged[['Country Name', 'Country Code', 'Year', 'Rural Value', 'Electricity Value']]

# Save the final dataframe to the specified path without the index
Target3_34.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_34/target_multisource.csv", index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read source CSV files with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
df0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_34/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
df1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_34/training_1.csv", index_col=0)

# UNPIVOT Source3_34_0: from wide year columns to long format with 'Year' and 'Rural Value'
df0_long = df0.melt(
    id_vars=['Country Name', 'Country Code', 'Indicator Name', 'Indicator Code'],
    var_name='Year',
    value_name='Rural Value'
)

# Filter df0_long to keep only rows where Indicator Name corresponds to rural population
df0_long = df0_long[df0_long['Indicator Name'] == 'Rural population (% of total population)']

# UNPIVOT Source3_34_1: from wide year columns to long format with 'Year' and 'Electricity Value'
df1_long = df1.melt(
    id_vars=['Country Name', 'Country Code', 'Indicator Name', 'Indicator Code'],
    var_name='Year',
    value_name='Electricity Value'
)

# Filter df1_long to keep only rows where Indicator Name corresponds to electricity access
df1_long = df1_long[df1_long['Indicator Name'] == 'Access to electricity (% of population)']

# Select only relevant columns for join
df0_sel = df0_long[['Country Name', 'Country Code', 'Year', 'Rural Value']]
df1_sel = df1_long[['Country Name', 'Country Code', 'Year', 'Electricity Value']]

# Join on Country Name, Country Code, and Year (all strings)
df_joined = pd.merge(
    df0_sel,
    df1_sel,
    how='inner',
    on=['Country Name', 'Country Code', 'Year']
)

# Convert Year to string to match target schema (if not already)
df_joined['Year'] = df_joined['Year'].astype(str)

# Remove rows with NaN in either Rural Value or Electricity Value
df_joined = df_joined.dropna(subset=['Rural Value', 'Electricity Value'])

# Group by Country Name, Country Code, Year and aggregate by max to remove duplicates if any
df_grouped = df_joined.groupby(
    ['Country Name', 'Country Code', 'Year'], as_index=False
).agg({
    'Rural Value': 'max',
    'Electricity Value': 'max'
})

# Convert Rural Value and Electricity Value to string to match target schema
df_grouped['Rural Value'] = df_grouped['Rural Value'].astype(str)
df_grouped['Electricity Value'] = df_grouped['Electricity Value'].astype(str)

# Write to target CSV
df_grouped.to_csv(
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_34/target_multisource_critique_history.csv",
    index=False
)
